A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DP-LLM work. Their text, equations, figures, tables and Appendices A–E are readable and support a complete comparison. The expanded bibliography accounts for v4's additional page.

before.justification: V2 reports original perplexity, downstream-task, latency and QoS measurements, together with ablations and decoding examples in Section 6 and Appendices B, C and E.

after.justification: V4 retains these original empirical results in Section 6 and Appendices B, C and E.

M1.justification: The three-phase precision and threshold assignment, training loss, hybrid relative-error estimator and asynchronous estimation are unchanged in Sections 3–5 and Algorithm 1.

E1.justification: Both versions use WikiText2, C4, GSM8K, MBPP, BBH, MATH-500 and Alpaca for the same calibration and evaluation tasks. No dataset, domain or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: LLM-MQ and HAWQ-V2 remain the evaluated static baselines, with unchanged formulations in Appendix B.2. The exact-estimator comparison and FP16 decoding examples also remain unchanged. Newly cited works are not added as experimental comparators.

E3.justification: The model configurations, precision and memory budgets, metrics, prompting settings, calibration samples and latency procedures are unchanged. Appendix B.1 retains 2048-token perplexity chunks, 5-shot GSM8K and 3-shot MBPP, BBH and MATH evaluation.

E4.justification: Both retain the exact-versus-approximate estimator analysis in Table 3, hybrid/asynchronous latency ablations in Table 6, precision-pair and calibration sensitivity studies in Appendix C, and the same decoding cases in Appendix E.

E5.justification: Appendix B.1 reports the same 10 latency-measurement repetitions. The estimator confidence statement and query-bitwidth percentile reporting are unchanged; no seed information, confidence intervals or significance tests are added.

E6.justification: Matched numerical results in Tables 1–14, plotted findings and decoding examples are unchanged. For example, Table 1 retains DP-LLM's Llama-3-8B perplexities of 6.59 on WikiText2 and 10.25 on C4 at target precision 4.0 under the 5-bit memory budget.

T1.justification: The relative-error definition, loss, Johnson–Lindenstrauss reasoning and Equations 1–9 are unchanged. Appendix A retains the same Taylor/Fisher approximation and integer-programming formulation; only associated citation numbers change.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the same claims about changing layer sensitivity, input-dependent precision selection, lightweight estimation and superior performance–latency trade-offs.

C2.justification: The explanations of performance, approximation quality and decoding examples are unchanged. Appendix D retains the decoding-only scope, exclusion of log-probability-only tasks and best-effort rather than guaranteed QoS limitation.

D1.justification: V4 supplies a gpt-fast repository reference, replacing unresolved citations in Section 6.2 and Appendix B.1. This adds an explicit access location for an already named implementation dependency. Hyperparameters, hardware, timing details and the DP-LLM repository link remain unchanged.

R1.justification: V4 adds four identifiable background references in Section 2.2: work on memory-frequency scaling, ApproxDet, LLM serving evaluation and DistServe. It also adds the gpt-fast reference. These resolve missing citations without changing the paper's novelty argument or relationship to competing precision-assignment methods.

P1.justification: V4 resolves citation placeholders, edits bibliography metadata and revises the acknowledgments, replacing the NRF grant acknowledgment with the IITP Global Scholars Invitation Program. The scientific prose, terminology and section structure remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The bibliography reflows onto an additional page, shifting the appendices, and repaired citations cause limited paragraph reflow. Figures 1–11 and Tables 1–14 retain their designs, captions, contents and relative placement.

improvement.justification: V4 resolves visible missing citations in Section 2.2, Section 6.2 and Appendix B.1, making background sources and the gpt-fast implementation dependency traceable. This provides a limited improvement in documentation quality; the methods, empirical evidence, analyses and limitations remain unchanged.
